Wouter Vrancken revealed he held a "one-on-one" talk with Sabri Guendouz as the Heart of Midlothian head coach expressed what he wanted from the creative midfielder.

Since joining from Beerschot for a significant six-figure fee in the summer, the Frenchman has largely been a peripheral figure after impressing in pre-season.

He has been an unused substitute in three of the last four Premiership games, as well as across the two-legged Conference League play-off tie with Rapid Vienna.

Vrancken explained the situation with Guendouz and why he has not been used in certain games off the bench.

"I've discussed it with the player, so he knows what to do. Last week, I had a one-on-one discussion with him, or talk with him, not a discussion, but a talk with him, pointing out what I want from him," he said.

The UK is in talks over rejoining EU security missions, in a move that would further widen Labour's "reset" in relations with Europe.

The agreement under negotiation could see British officials and experts take part in civilian crisis management operations for the first time since Brexit.

EU is currently conducting 13 crisis management missions from a permanent HQ based in Brussels, as part of its common foreign and security policy.

They span efforts to train Somalian coastguards in tackling piracy, advise border police in Mali, and help Ukrainian prosecutors investigate war crime allegations.

Cybersecurity support to help countries protect themselves from hacking has been a priority area in recent years, with dedicated operations in Moldova and Armenia.
